body: The issue occurs for navigation polygons with counter-clockwise vertex winding order. clockwise|counterclockwise -|- | Tiles|Generated polygon -|- | Test project: [bug-report---flipped-tile_v2.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24476640/bug-report---flipped-tile_v2.zip) An odd number of enabled `flip_h`/`flip_v`/`transpose` cell flags results in changing the vertex winding order compared to the original polygon (if we only transform the vertices). In such cases the vertex order would need to be reversed to preserve the original winding order. For physics collisions/obstacles the winding order does not affect the result. @smix8 I'm not sure if this is an issue within the NavigationServer parsing/generation and needs to be fixed in there, or whether the proper winding order needs to be ensured in the TileMapLayer/TileSet providing the polygon data. But given collision polygons are excluded from the result just fine regardless of the winding order, I suspect `NavigationMeshSourceGeometryData2D::_add_traversable_outline` should also work properly regardless of its input winding order (like `NavigationMeshSourceGeometryData2D::_add_obstruction_outline` seems to work). https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/76dda5c6c50c9cc26128c5e831f1a70b6e8a6785/scene/2d/tile_map_layer.cpp#L3558-L3615

> The TileMap editor needs to assure valid outline output.

The thing is, I don't think it's fully possible given how the generation works currently. If the user would add an outline enclosing tiles' navigation polygons (like in the MRP here), then the tile polygons will be considered as holes/not holes depending on their winding order compared to the enclosing outline's winding order.

Preserving the tile's polygon original winding order regardless of its flips/transpose is easy, will open a PR. But the tile still can end up considered to be a hole if enclosed in outline with different winding order.

Note that [navigation mesh script template from the docs](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/tutorials/navigation/navigation_using_navigationmeshes.html#navigation-mesh-script-templates) suggests adding such "boundary" outline, maybe it should be made clearer that doing so if the TileMapLayer itself provides the navigation polygons can result in holes in case of winding order mismatch? 🤔
```gdscript
func on_parsing_done() -> void:
	# If we did not parse a TileMap with navigation mesh cells we may now only
	# have obstruction outlines so add at least one traversable outline
	# so the obstructions outlines have something to "cut" into.
	source_geometry.add_traversable_outline(PackedVector2Array([
		Vector2(0.0, 0.0),
		Vector2(500.0, 0.0),
		Vector2(500.0, 500.0),
		Vector2(0.0, 500.0)
	]))
```

> Note that navigation mesh script template from the docs suggests adding such "boundary" outline

Yes because except for weird TileMap cases were the legacy build-in navmesh is used you always need at least something to "cut" your obstruction objects into or nothing will happen.
